# Results — Study 879 (Weekly Economic Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
**Weekly Economic Index** (Lewis, Mertens & Stock, 2020), a real-time weekly activity
nowcast, should let its **level** and its **weekly change** time **forward SPY** and the
**cyclical-vs-defensive rotation** (XLY vs XLP): a higher / rising nowcast → higher forward
return and cyclical outperformance. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped) — all numbers are stamped
as-of 2026-06-30. Fingerprint `94e9e76c22ef` (WEI level & weekly change).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real nowcast | **Dallas Fed WEI workbook** (`weekly-economic-index.xlsx`, `2008-current` sheet), current-vintage weekly WEI, week-ending Saturdays 2008-01-05 → 2026-06-27 (sliced to as-of) |
| Real returns | **SPY / XLY / XLP** daily total-return closes (yfinance, `auto_adjust=True`), through 2026-06-30 |
| Aligned frame | **962** weekly rows, 2008-01-12 → 2026-06-13, columns `wei` (level), `dwei` (weekly change), forward SPY (`spy_h1`/`spy_h4`) and forward XLY−XLP rotation (`rot_h1`/`rot_h4`) |
| Signal | current-vintage WEI **level** and its **week-over-week change**, standardized (full-sample z; a HAC slope *t* is scale-invariant) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: a week-ending-Saturday nowcast is only *published* the next week, so every forward return is anchored **one trading week (5 days) later** — the position is taken after the nowcast is known. Rotation overlay charges one-way cost/leg on turnover + 50 bps/yr borrow on the short |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, Bartlett, 8-lag) *t* on the predictive-regression slopes; univariate + joint; a two-era cut (split 2017-01-01); a 2,000-draw permutation placebo; a costed rotation overlay; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The nowcast side is the WEI as revised (the
current vintage); a strictly real-time test would use the vintage available *each week*.
Revisions to the WEI are small relative to its weekly change, and we act with a one-week
publication lag, but the level result carries a mild look-ahead caveat, so the **level**
magnitudes are an upper bound. SPY/XLY/XLP are current, index-tracking ETFs (no delisting).

## The headline — predictive regression (Newey-West HAC *t*)

Forward return regressed on a constant + standardized WEI level & weekly change (joint;
univariate *t* in parentheses):

| target | n | R² | level *t* | weekly-change *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY, 1 week** | 962 | 0.003 | **−1.12** (−0.96) | **+1.34** (+1.16) |
| **SPY, 4 weeks** | 959 | 0.011 | −1.76 (−1.71) | +0.69 (+0.39) |
| **XLY−XLP, 1 week** | 962 | 0.005 | −1.88 (−1.81) | +0.75 (+0.58) |
| **XLY−XLP, 4 weeks** | 959 | 0.020 | **−2.24** (−2.22) | +0.06 (−0.21) |

The claim **does not hold.** On forward **SPY** the WEI **level** is *insignificant and
carries the wrong sign* (t = −1.12), and the **weekly change** — the theoretically-right
timing signal — is the right sign but **insignificant** (t = +1.34). The only slope that
crosses |t| ≥ 2 anywhere is the **rotation level at 4 weeks (t = −2.24)** — and it is
**wrong-signed**: a *higher* nowcast predicts cyclical (XLY) *under*-performance vs
defensives (XLP), the opposite of "strong growth → buy cyclicals." That is a
mean-reversion pattern (cyclicals that have already run when growth is hot give some back),
not the claimed nowcast edge. R² never exceeds ~2%.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2017-01-01), univariate HAC *t*

| target | early (2008–2016) | late (2017–2026) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **SPY 1wk** — level | +0.45 | **−2.69** |
| **SPY 1wk** — weekly change | **+2.26** | +0.24 |
| **XLY−XLP 4wk** — level | −0.59 | **−2.52** |
| **XLY−XLP 4wk** — weekly change | +0.73 | −0.45 |

Nothing is era-stable *with the right sign*. The one genuinely claim-consistent hit — the
weekly change predicting SPY, **t = +2.26** — lives **entirely in 2008–2016** and
evaporates post-2017 (**t = +0.24**). That early window is dominated by the 2008–09
recession and the sharp recovery: the WEI's apparent timing power is the one-off
crash-and-rebound cycle, exactly the confound. The wrong-signed pieces (SPY-level,
rotation-level) are concentrated in the *late* era.

## Conditional — forward return when the nowcast is 'on' vs the base rate

| condition | conditional | base rate | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY 1wk \| WEI above median | +0.26% (win 61%) | +0.24% | +0.17 |
| SPY 1wk \| weekly change > 0 | +0.40% (win 61%) | +0.24% | +1.22 |
| XLY−XLP 4wk \| WEI above median | +0.05% (win 52%) | +0.36% | −1.16 |

A rising nowcast is *directionally* associated with a slightly higher next-week SPY return
(+0.40% vs +0.24%), but the gap is well inside noise (Welch t = +1.22). Conditioning the
rotation on a high WEI *lowers* forward cyclical performance (−1.16) — again the wrong way.

## Placebo — is the (wrong-signed) rotation slope a lucky alignment?

Permute the WEI, re-run the univariate HAC slope *t* on `rot_h4`, 2,000 draws:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed \|t\| | **2.22** |
| placebo mean \|t\| | 0.80 |
| two-sided p | **0.026** |

The wrong-signed rotation relation is beyond the permutation cloud (p ≈ 0.03), i.e. it is a
*real* mean-reversion effect — but it is the **opposite** of the claim, so it cannot stamp
the nowcast edge as present.

## The timer — costed long-cyclical / short-defensive (XLY−XLP) overlay, weekly

Position from the nowcast sign (one-week lag already in the forward leg); one-way 5 bps/leg
on turnover + 50 bps/yr borrow on the short:

| signal / rule | gross Sharpe | net Sharpe | vs always-hold | net ann. | *t*(net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| WEI above median | −0.11 | **−0.16** | +0.28 | −2.8%/yr | −0.71 |
| weekly change > 0 | +0.21 | **+0.02** | +0.28 | +0.3%/yr | +0.07 |

Both overlays **lose to simply holding the rotation** (Sharpe +0.28). The WEI-level rule is
outright negative; the weekly-change rule earns a thin gross Sharpe (+0.21) that its 1,123
weekly turns wipe out to +0.02 net. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded weekly frame with a planted WEI→forward-return relation. No network.

| world | level *t* (SPY) |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.13** (sd 1.12), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** (≈5% false-positive rate) |
| planted (`edge = 0.010`, seed 879) | **+16.69** (rotation level *t* = +22.05) |

The detector recovers a planted nowcast edge cleanly and fires on the null at the expected
~5% rate — so the null real-tape result is a genuine absence of the claimed effect, not a
broken test. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** A weekly growth nowcast does **not** beat the monthly tape here. The
  WEI **level** does not predict forward SPY (t = −1.12, wrong sign) and is era-unstable
  (late t = −2.69); the **weekly change** has the right sign but is **insignificant** overall
  (t = +1.34) and its only |t| ≥ 2 hit (SPY, early era, +2.26) is a one-off artefact of the
  2008–09 recession/recovery that **vanishes post-2017**. The single overall |t| ≥ 2 slope —
  rotation level, 4-week, **t = −2.24**, placebo p = 0.026 — is **wrong-signed** (high growth
  → cyclical *under*-performance, a mean-reversion), which cannot support the claim. No
  robust, right-signed, era-stable predictor exists.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The costed long-cyclical / short-defensive overlay
  under-performs simply holding the rotation (net Sharpe −0.16 / +0.02 vs +0.28), the thin
  weekly-change edge eaten entirely by rebalancing friction.
